newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn gold plan is "problematic"-German banks.
newsitem.headline: Bonn gold plan is "problematic"-German banks.

text.p: A group representing Germany's largest private banks said on Friday Bonn's plan to revalue gold reserves was problematic, and said a rift with the Bundesbank could damage Germany's reputation.
The Federal Association of German Banks (VdB) said in its monthly report that revaluing gold and currency reserves alone was no unusual measure.
But it said Bonn's "intended, premature payout of a part of the book profit" in 1997 was "extraordinary."
The Bundesbank's next regularly scheduled profit payout was supposed to be in early 1998, VdB said.
On Wednesday the Bundesbank rejected Bonn's plan to revalue gold and possibly also currency reserves to help narrow the federal budget deficit to qualify for European monetary union.
The government responded by saying it would move ahead with the plan anyway.

Bonn and the Bundesbank should work together before "to find a solution that neither hurts the reputation of German money policy ... nor creates a burden for the stability-oriented start of monetary union," BdB said.
The arrival of the plan only about a week after Bonn said tax revenues would fall well below targets left the impression that German budget policy was undergoing "an emergency operation," VdB said.
But it also noted that other governments have revalued reserves and Germany's current gold valuation was below the prices used by all but on European Union member.
